paragraphs: References herein to "we," "us," "our," the "Company," and "Penumbra," refer to Penumbra, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries unless expressly indicated or the context requires otherwise.

Penumbra, the world's leading thrombectomy company, is focused on developing the most innovative technologies for challenging medical conditions such as ischemic stroke, venous thromboembolism such as pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia. Our broad portfolio, which includes computer assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT), centers on removing blood clots from head-to-toe with speed, safety, and simplicity. Our team focuses on developing, manufacturing and marketing novel products for use by specialist physicians and other healthcare providers to drive improved clinical and health outcomes. We believe that the cost-effectiveness of our products is attractive to our customers.

Since our founding in 2004, we have invested heavily in our product development and commercial expansion that has established the foundation of our global organization. We have successfully developed, obtained regulatory clearance or approval for, and introduced products into the thrombectomy market since 2007, access market since 2008, embolization market since 2011, and neurosurgical market since 2014.

We expect to continue to develop and build our portfolio of products, including our thrombectomy, embolization, and access technologies, while iterating on our currently available products. Generally, when we introduce a next generation product or a new product designed to replace a current product, sales of the earlier generation product or the product replaced decline. Our research and development activities are centered around the development of new products and clinical activities designed to support our regulatory submissions and demonstrate the effectiveness of our products.

We attribute our success to our culture built on cooperation, our highly efficient product innovation process, our disciplined approach to product and commercial development, our deep understanding of our target end markets and our relationships with specialist physicians and other healthcare providers. We believe these factors have enabled us to rapidly innovate in a highly efficient manner.

We sell our products to healthcare providers primarily through our direct sales organization in the United States, most of Europe, Canada, Australia and Singapore, as well as through distributors in select international markets. We generated revenue of $1,403.7 million, $1,194.6 million and $1,058.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. This represents an annual increase of 17.5% and 12.9%, respectively. We generated income from operations of $189.2 million, $9.3 million and $73.6 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

During the year ended December 31, 2024, we made the strategic decision to wind down and exit our immersive healthcare business, and as a result we incurred $115.3 million in impairment and other charges in connection with this decision. Refer to Note "4. Exit of Immersive Healthcare Business" to our consolidated financial statements in Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K. In addition, during the year ended December 31, 2024, we permanently ceased sales of our immersive healthcare products and related commercial operations. There were no impairment or other charges in connection with the wind down and exit of our immersive healthcare business during the year ended December 31, 2025.

On January 14, 2026, we entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the "Merger Agreement") with Boston Scientific Corporation, a Delaware corporation, and Pinehurst Merger Sub, Inc. ("Merger Sub"), a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Boston Scientific Corporation, pursuant to which Boston Scientific Corporation has agreed to acquire us in a transaction (the "Merger") reflecting an enterprise value of approximately $14.5 billion. Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, which has been approved by the board of directors of each of the Company and Boston Scientific Corporation, the transaction values each share of our common stock at $374 per share, with our stockholders having the right to elect, for each share of our common stock held by them, to receive $374 in cash or 3.8721 shares of Boston Scientific Corporation's common stock (valued at $374 based on the volume weighted average price of Boston Scientific Corporation's common stock over the 10 trading days ending January 13, 2026), subject to proration, so that the total transaction consideration is paid approximately 73% in cash and approximately 27% in shares of Boston Scientific Corporation's common stock. The Merger is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to customary closing conditions, including approval by our stockholders and regulatory approvals. See Note "20. Subsequent Events" to our consolidated financial statements in Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K for more information.

We concentrate on improving treatment outcomes for patients with certain forms of vascular disease. Vascular disease refers to any condition that affects the circulatory system and typically manifests as a blockage or rupture of an artery or a vein. When the treatment for vascular disease is performed from within a vessel, it is referred to as an endovascular procedure. Historically, we classified our end markets according to the anatomic location of the disorder and divided them into neuro, which included neurovascular and neurosurgical, and vascular, which included peripheral vascular and cardiovascular. To better align with our strategic priorities, beginning with the three months ended December 31, 2023 we began to classify our end markets based on the type of procedure being performed, and therefore divide our markets into thrombectomy, which includes products that treat conditions such as pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis, acute limb ischemia, ischemic stroke and coronary disease, and embolization and access, which include products to treat aneurysms and to occlude vessels as well as products to access the vasculature.

We generated revenue of $947.9 million, $815.5 million and $677.3 million from our thrombectomy product category for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. We generated revenue of $455.7 million, $379.1 million, and $381.2 million from our embolization and access product categories for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. The Company designs, develops, manufactures and markets novel products, and operates as one operating segment.

While reliable third-party data is not available for many markets outside the United States, we believe there are substantial additional market opportunities for our thrombectomy and embolization and access products throughout the world.

The thrombectomy market is comprised of vascular diseases and disorders occurring in vessels throughout the body, including ischemic stroke, venous thromboembolism such as pulmonary embolism, acute limb ischemia, deep vein thrombosis, coronary disease and other conditions. Disruption of blood flow to the vasculature can have serious adverse consequences, including death and morbidity, and our solutions address the intervention of these diseases. There are approximately 2.15 million incidences of clot in the vasculature each year in the United States, the vast majority of which do not currently receive mechanical thrombectomy intervention. Studies have shown that patients treated with mechanical thrombectomy had improved functional outcomes compared with treatments such as tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA) alone.
Some of the more common conditions we focus on are:

•Pulmonary Embolism ("PE"): PE is a condition that occurs when blood clots, which typically travel from the veins in the legs, get caught in the lungs. Approximately 1.2 million PEs occur annually worldwide. In the U.S., there are approximately 350,000 PEs per year causing approximately 50,000 annual deaths according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. High- and intermediate-risk PEs, which are generally eligible for treatment with mechanical or computer assisted vacuum thrombectomy, represent approximately 44% of such PEs, or approximately 150,000 U.S. patients. We estimate there are approximately 800,000 annual PEs outside the U.S. and approximately 350,000 of them are high- or intermediate-risk, making them eligible for thrombectomy.

headings: Risk Related to Our Proposed Merger
Uncertainty associated with our agreement to be acquired by Boston Scientific Corporation could have an adverse effect on our business.
The failure to complete the Merger could adversely affect our business.
We will continue to incur substantial transaction-related costs in connection with the Merger.
We and our directors and officers may be subject to lawsuits relating to the Merger.
Provisions of the Merger Agreement may deter alternative business combinations and could negatively impact our stock price if the Merger Agreement is terminated in certain circumstances.

Because the market price of Boston Scientific Corporation common stock may fluctuate, holders of our common stock cannot be certain of the market value of the consideration they will receive in the Merger.
Our existing products may be rendered obsolete and we may be unable to effectively introduce and market new products or may fail to keep pace with advances in technology.
We face significant competition, and if we are unable to compete effectively, we may not be able to achieve or maintain significant market penetration or improve our results of operations.
We may not be able to achieve or maintain satisfactory pricing and margins for our products.
We may not have the resources to successfully market and sell our products, which would adversely affect our business and results of operations.
Third-party reimbursement may not be available or adequate for the procedures or sessions for which our products are used, and may be subject to change.
Our dependence on key suppliers puts us at risk of interruptions in the availability of our products, which could reduce our revenue and adversely affect our results of operations.
We cannot be certain that we will be able to manufacture our products in high volumes at commercially reasonable costs.
We are required to maintain high levels of inventory, which consume a significant amount of our working capital and could lead to permanent write-downs or write-offs of our inventory.

Defects or failures or alleged defects or failures associated with our products could lead to recalls, safety alerts, or product-related or securities litigation, as well as significant costs and negative publicity.

Negative publicity regarding our products or marketing tactics by competitors or other third parties could reduce demand for our products, which would adversely affect sales and our financial performance.
To successfully market and sell our products internationally, we must address a number of unique challenges applicable to international markets.
We rely on our distributors to market and sell our products in certain international markets.
Foreign currency exchange rates may adversely affect our results.
We have experienced rapid growth in recent periods, and if we fail to manage our growth effectively, our business and results of operations may suffer.

Because our business is subject to many risks and our actual results may differ materially from any forward-looking statements made by or on behalf of us, this section includes a discussion of important factors that could affect our business, operating results, financial condition and the trading price of our common stock. You should carefully consider these risk factors, together with all of the other information included in this Form 10-K as well as our other publicly available filings with the SEC. If any of the following risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition, results of operations and future prospects could be materially and adversely harmed.

Uncertainty about the effect of the Merger Agreement and the Merger on our customers, employees, suppliers, vendors, and business partners may have an adverse effect on our business and operations that may be material to our company. For example, our employees may experience uncertainty about their roles following the Merger. There can be no assurance we will be able to attract and retain key talent, including senior leaders, engineers, salespeople, and others to the same extent that we have previously been able to attract and retain employees. Any loss or distraction of such employees could have a material adverse effect on our business and operations. In addition, we have diverted, and will continue to divert, significant management attention and resources towards the completion of the Merger, which could materially adversely affect our business and results of operations.

Moreover, our customers may experience uncertainty associated with the Merger, including with respect to possible changes to our products, technology or policies. Similarly, our suppliers, vendors, business partners and distribution channels may experience uncertainty associated with the Merger, including with respect to current or future business relationships with us. Uncertainty may cause customers to refrain from purchasing our products and to instead purchase our competitors' products, and suppliers, vendors and business partners may seek to change existing business relationships, which could result in an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition in a way that may be material to our company.

Pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement, until the Merger becomes effective or the Merger Agreement is terminated, we are subject to certain restrictions on the conduct of our business, including in certain cases restrictions on our ability to enter into certain material contracts, acquire or dispose of assets outside of the ordinary course of business, incur indebtedness or make unbudgeted capital expenditures. These restrictions may prevent us from taking actions with respect to our business that we may consider advantageous, and result in our inability to respond effectively to competitive pressures and industry developments and may otherwise harm our business and results of operations.

Completion of the Merger is subject to conditions beyond our control that may prevent, delay or otherwise adversely affect its completion in a material way, including the approval of our stockholders and the expiration or termination of applicable waiting periods and the receipt of certain clearances under antitrust and competition laws. If the Merger or a similar transaction is not completed, the share price of our common stock may decline to the extent that the current market price of our common stock reflects an assumption that a transaction will be completed. In addition, under circumstances defined in the Merger Agreement, we may be required to pay Boston Scientific Corporation a termination fee of $525.0 million in the event the Merger is not completed. Further, a failure to complete the Merger may result in negative publicity for us in the investment community. Any disruption to our business resulting from the announcement and pendency of the Merger, including any adverse changes in our relationships with our customers, suppliers, vendors and business partners could continue or accelerate in the event of a failure to complete the Merger. There can be no assurance that our business, these relationships or our financial condition will not be adversely affected if the Merger is not consummated.

There are a number of factors that have impacted, and we believe will continue to impact, our results of operations and growth. These factors include:
•The rate at which we grow our salesforce and the speed at which newly hired salespeople become fully effective can impact our revenue growth or our costs incurred in anticipation of such growth.

•Our industry is intensely competitive and, in particular, we compete with a number of large, well-capitalized companies. We must continue to successfully compete in light of our competitors' existing and future products and their resources to successfully market to the specialist physicians who use our products.

•We must continue to successfully introduce new products that gain acceptance with specialist physicians and other healthcare providers and successfully transition from existing products to new products, ensuring adequate supply. In addition, as we introduce new products and expand our production capacity, we anticipate additional personnel will be hired and trained to build our inventory of components and finished goods in advance of sales, which may cause quarterly fluctuations in our operating results and financial condition.

paragraphs: herein 所稱 "we," "us," "our," the "Company," 及 "Penumbra," 指 Penumbra, Inc. 及其合併子公司，除非另有明確說明或上下文另有要求。

Penumbra 是全球領先的血栓切除術公司，專注於開發用以治療如缺血性中風、靜脈血栓栓塞症（如肺栓塞）及急性肢體缺血等困難醫療狀況的最創新技術。我們的廣泛產品組合，包括電腦輔助真空血栓切除術（CAVT），專注於以速度、安全性和簡易性從頭到腳移除血塊。我們的團隊專注於開發、製造及行銷用以供專科醫師及其他醫療提供者使用的創新產品，以推動改善臨牀及健康結果。我們相信我們產品的成本效益對客戶而言具有吸引力。
自 2004 年成立以來，我們已大量投資於產品開發及商業擴張，奠定了我們全球組織的基礎。自 2007 年起，我們已成功開發、取得監管核准或批准，並推出產品至血栓切除術市場；自 2008 年起進入市場；自 2011 年起進入栓塞市場；自 2014 年起進入神經外科市場。
我們預期將持續開發並建立我們的產品組合，包括我們的血栓切除術、栓塞及進入技術，同時對目前可提供的產品進行改進。通常，當我們推出新一代產品或設計用以取代現有產品的新產品時，較早一代產品或被取代產品的銷售會下降。我們的研究與開發活動主要圍繞新產品的開發及臨牀活動，以支持我們的監管申請並展示我們產品的成效。
我們的成功歸功於我們以合作為基礎的文化、高度高效的產品創新流程、對產品及商業開發的嚴謹方法、對目標終端市場的深入理解，以及與專科醫師及其他醫療提供者之間的關係。我們相信這些因素使我們能夠以高度效率快速創新。

於截至2024年12月31日的會計年度，我們做出戰略決定，逐步終止並退出沉浸式醫療業務，因此與此決定相關，我們產生115.3 百萬美元的減值及其他費用。請參閱本Form 10-K第二部分，第8項「財務報表」中附註「4. 沉浸式醫療業務退出」。此外，於截至2024年12月31日的會計年度，我們永久終止銷售沉浸式醫療產品及相關商業運作。於截至2025年12月31日的會計年度，與我們沉浸式醫療業務的終止及退出無關的減值及其他費用為零。

2026 年 1 月 14 日，我們與 Boston Scientific Corporation（一間 Delaware 州公司）及 Pinehurst Merger Sub, Inc.（"Merger Sub"，一間 Delaware 州公司，為 Boston Scientific Corporation 的 wholly owned 子公司）簽訂合併協議（"Merger Agreement"），根據該協議，Boston Scientific Corporation 同意以交易（"Merger"）收購我們，該交易反映企業價值約為 145 億美元。根據 Merger Agreement 的條款，該交易已獲本公司及 Boston Scientific Corporation 董事會批准，交易中每一股我們的普通股價值為 374 美元，股東可選擇以現金 374 美元或 3.8721 股 Boston Scientific Corporation 的普通股（根據 2026 年 1 月 13 日前 10 個交易日 Boston Scientific Corporation 普通股市場成交量加權平均價格計算，價值為 374 美元）換取，並根據比例調整，使交易總對價約 73% 以現金支付，約 27% 以 Boston Scientific Corporation 普通股支付。該合併預計於 2026 年底前完成，需符合常見的關閉條件，包括股東批准及監管批准。請參閱本 Form 10-K 第二部分，第 8 項「財務報表」中「20. 後續事件」的附註以取得更多資訊。

本公司致力於改善特定血管疾病患者之治療成效。血管疾病係指影響循環系統之任何狀況，通常表現為動脈或靜脈之阻塞或破裂。當血管疾病之治療係從血管內進行時，稱為內血管手術。歷史來看，本公司將終端市場依疾病之解剖位置分類，並分為神經類，包含神經血管及神經外科，以及血管類，包含外周血管及心血管。為更好地符合本公司戰略優先順序，自2023年12月31日結帳週期起，本公司開始依執行之手術類型分類終端市場，因此將市場分為血栓切除術，包含用以治療肺栓塞、深靜脈血栓、急性肢體缺血、缺血性中風及冠狀動脈疾病等狀況之產品，以及栓塞與通路，包含用以治療動脈瘤及封閉血管之產品，以及用以接觸血管系統之產品。
本公司於2025年12月31日結帳年度，於血栓切除術產品類別中產生營業收入947.9百萬美元，2024年為815.5百萬美元，2023年為677.3百萬美元。本公司於2025年12月31日結帳年度，於栓塞與通路產品類別中產生營業收入455.7百萬美元，2024年為379.1百萬美元，2023年為381.2百萬美元。本公司設計、開發、製造及行銷創新產品，並作為一個營運分部運作。
雖然許多美國以外市場缺乏可靠第三方資料，本公司認為全球範圍內仍有相當多的市場機會，可供本公司之血栓切除術及栓塞與通路產品應用。

血栓切除術市場包含發生於全身血管之血管疾病及狀況，包括缺血性中風、靜脈血栓栓塞症（如肺栓塞）、急性肢體缺血、深靜脈血栓、冠狀動脈疾病及其他狀況。血液流動至血管系統受擾可能導致嚴重後果，包括死亡及病態，而本公司之解決方案針對這些疾病之介入進行處理。美國每年約有215萬例血管內血栓形成，其中絕大多數目前尚未接受機械血栓切除術介入。研究顯示，接受機械血栓切除術治療之患者，其功能成效較單獨使用組織型纖維蛋白溶酶原活化劑（tPA）治療者為佳。
本公司較常關注之某些狀況為：
•肺栓塞（"PE"）：肺栓塞係指血液凝塊，通常來自腿部靜脈，阻塞肺部之狀況。全球每年約有120萬例肺栓塞。根據疾病管制中心資料，美國每年約有35萬例肺栓塞，導致約5萬人死亡。高風險及中風險肺栓塞，通常可接受機械或電腦輔助真空血栓切除術治療，約佔總肺栓塞數量的44%，即約15萬名美國患者。本公司估計，美國以外每年約有80萬例肺栓塞，其中約35萬例為高風險或中風險，使其符合血栓切除術治療條件。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析，並與本表單 10-K 所包含之合併財務報表及相關附註一併參考。本討論與本報告之其他部分包含風險與不確定性之預測性陳述，例如我們之計畫、目標、預期與意圖之陳述。由於許多因素，包括本表單 10-K 之「風險因素」部分所列之因素，我們之實際結果可能與預測性陳述中所描述或暗示之結果有重大差異。有關我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年營運成果與 2023 年 12 月 31 日財年營運成果之比較之討論，請參閱我們 2024 年 12 月 31 日財年年度報告表單 10-K 之第二部分，第 7 項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」，於 2025 年 2 月 18 日提交至 SEC，並已納入本表單 10-K。
本文件中所稱「我們」、「我們」、「我們」、「公司」及「Penumbra」，均指 Penumbra, Inc. 及其合併子公司，除非另有明確說明或上下文另有要求。
Penumbra 是全球領先之血栓切除術公司，專注於開發用以處理如缺血性中風、靜脈血栓栓塞（如肺栓塞）及急性肢體缺血等困難醫療狀況之最創新技術。我們廣泛之產品組合，包括電腦輔助真空血栓切除術（CAVT），專注於以速度、安全性與簡易性從頭到腳移除血栓。我們團隊專注於開發、製造與行銷創新產品，供專科醫師及其他醫療提供者使用，以提升臨牀與健康結果。我們相信我們產品之成本效益對客戶而言具有吸引力。
自 2004 年成立以來，我們已大量投資於產品開發與商業擴張，奠定了我們全球組織的基礎。自 2007 年起，我們已成功開發、取得監管核准或批准，並推出產品至血栓切除術市場；自 2008 年起進入市場；自 2011 年起進入栓塞市場；自 2014 年起進入神經外科市場。
我們預期將持續開發與建立產品組合，包括我們之血栓切除術、栓塞及進入技術，同時對目前可提供之產品進行改進。通常，當我們推出新一代產品或設計用以取代現有產品之新產品時，較早一代產品或被取代產品之銷售會下降。我們之研究與開發活動專注於新產品之開發與臨牀活動，以支持我們之監管申請並展示我們產品之有效性。
我們將成功歸因於我們建立在合作文化之上之組織、我們高度效率之產品創新流程、我們對產品與商業開發之嚴謹方法、我們對目標終端市場之深入理解，以及我們與專科醫師及其他醫療提供者之關係。我們相信這些因素使我們能以高度效率快速創新。

於2024年12月31日財務年度，我們做出戰略決策，逐步關閉並退出沉浸式醫療業務，因此與此決策相關，我們產生115.3 百萬美元的減值及其它費用。請參閱本Form 10-K第二部分，第8項「財務報表」中附註「4. 沉浸式醫療業務退出」以取得更多細節。於2024年12月31日財務年度，我們永久停止銷售沉浸式醫療產品及相關商業運作。於2025年12月31日財務年度，與我們沉浸式醫療業務的關閉及退出無關的減值或其它費用為零。

於 2026 年 1 月 14 日，本公司與 Boston Scientific Corporation 及 Merger Sub 簽訂合併協議，根據該協議，Boston Scientific Corporation 同意透過合併方式收購本公司，交易總企業價值約為 145 億美元。根據合併協議條款，該協議已獲本公司與 Boston Scientific Corporation 董事會批准，交易每一股本公司普通股價值為 374 美元，本公司股東可選擇，針對其所持有的每一股本公司普通股，以現金 374 美元或 3.8721 股 Boston Scientific Corporation 普通股（根據 2026 年 1 月 13 日前 10 個交易日 Boston Scientific Corporation 普通股成交量加權平均價格計算，價值為 374 美元）進行兌換，並經比例調整後，使總交易對價約為 73% 以現金支付，約為 27% 以 Boston Scientific 普通股支付。
該合併預計於 2026 年底前完成，但需符合慣常的交割條件，包括本公司股東批准及監管機關核准。有關更多資訊，請參閱本 Form 10-K 第二部分第 8 項「綜合財務報表」附註「20. 後續事件」。
有許多因素已影響，且本公司認為將持續影響，我們的營運成果與成長。這些因素包括：
•我們銷售團隊的成長速度以及新進銷售人員成為完全有效率的時間，可能影響我們的營收成長或我們預期成長所產生的成本。
•我們的產業競爭激烈，尤其與許多資金雄厚的大公司競爭。我們必須持續成功競爭，以應對競爭對手現有及未來的產品及其資源，以有效行銷給使用我們產品的專科醫師。
•我們必須持續成功推出新產品，使其獲得專科醫師及其他醫療提供者的接受，並成功從現有產品轉換為新產品，確保供應充足。此外，隨著我們推出新產品並擴充生產能力，我們預期將聘請並培訓更多人員，以建立零組件及成品的庫存，以備銷售之用，這可能會導致我們每季營運成果與財務狀況產生波動。

headings: 與我們擬議合併相關的風險
與我們同意被 Boston Scientific Corporation 收購的協議相關的不確定性，可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
未能完成合併可能會對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們將持續產生與合併相關的重大交易費用。
我們與董事及高階管理人員可能因合併而面臨訴訟。
合併協議的條款可能會阻礙其他業務組合，若在特定情況下合併協議終止，可能會對我們的股票價格產生負面影響。
由於 Boston Scientific Corporation 普通股的市場價格可能波動，我們普通股的持有人無法確定他們在合併中將收到的對價之市場價值。
本公司現有產品可能變得過時，本公司可能無法有效推出及行銷新產品，或無法跟上技術進步的節奏。
本公司面臨激烈的競爭，若本公司無法有效競爭，可能無法達成或維持顯著的市場佔有率，或改善本公司營運成果。
本公司可能無法達成或維持產品的滿意價格與毛利率。
本公司可能缺乏足夠資源成功行銷與銷售產品，這將對本公司業務與營運成果造成不利影響。
第三方報銷可能無法提供或足夠用於本公司產品所使用的程序或會談，且可能受到變動影響。
本公司對關鍵供應商的依賴，使本公司面臨產品供應中斷的風險，這可能會減少本公司收入，並對本公司營運成果造成不利影響。
本公司無法確定是否能以商業上合理的成本大量製造產品。
本公司必須維持高水準的存貨，這會消耗本公司大量營運資金，並可能導致存貨的永久減值或減損。
產品若存在瑕疵或故障，或被指控存在瑕疵或故障，可能會導致產品回收、安全警示、與產品相關或證券的訴訟，以及產生重大成本與負面宣傳。
關於我們產品或行銷策略的負面宣傳，由競爭對手或其他第三方所發起，可能會降低產品需求，進而對銷售與財務表現產生不利影響。
為成功行銷與銷售我們的產品至國際市場，我們必須解決適用於國際市場的多項獨特挑戰。
我們依賴經銷商在某些國際市場行銷與銷售我們的產品。
外幣匯率變動可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
我們在近期經歷了快速成長，若未能有效管理成長，將可能影響我們的業務與營運成果。
paragraphs: 本表10-K 係基於我們目前預期所載之向前看資訊。由於我們的業務面臨許多風險，且實際結果可能與任何向前看聲明有重大差異，本節包含可能影響我們業務、營運結果、財務狀況及普通股交易價格的重要因素討論。您應謹慎考量這些風險因素，並與本表10-K 所包含的所有其他資訊以及我們向SEC公開的其他文件一併考量。若任何下列風險實際發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果及未來展望造成重大且不利的影響。

於2026年1月14日，我們與波士頓科學公司及合併子公司簽訂合併協議，根據協議，波士頓科學公司同意以每股374美元收購我們，我們股東可選擇以現金374美元或波士頓科學公司普通股3.8721股（以2026年1月13日結訖之10個交易日波士頓科學公司普通股成交量加權平均價格計算，價值為374美元）換取其持有的每股普通股，經比例調整後，總交易對價約有73%以現金支付，約有27%以波士頓科學公司普通股支付。對於合併協議及合併對我們客戶、員工、供應商、經銷商及業務夥伴的影響存在不確定性，可能對我們的業務及營運造成不利影響，且可能對我們公司產生重大影響。例如，我們的員工可能在合併後對其職務角色產生不確定性。我們無法保證能像以往一樣吸引並留住關鍵人才，包括高階主管、工程師、業務人員及其他人員。若失去或分散這些員工，可能對我們的業務及營運造成重大不利影響。此外，我們已轉移並會持續轉移大量管理注意力及資源至合併的完成，這可能對我們的業務及營運結果造成重大不利影響。

此外，我們的客戶可能因合併而產生不確定性，包括對我們產品、技術或政策可能變動的擔憂。同樣地，我們的供應商、經銷商、業務夥伴及經銷通路也可能因合併而產生不確定性，包括對與我們現有或未來業務關係的擔憂。不確定性可能導致客戶避免購買我們的產品，而改為購買競爭對手的產品，供應商、經銷商及業務夥伴可能尋求改變現有業務關係，這可能導致對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響，且可能對我們公司產生重大影響。
根據合併協議的條款，直至合併生效或協議終止前，我們的業務運作受到某些限制，包括在某些情況下限制我們簽訂重大契約、取得或處置非日常業務範疇的資產、負擔債務或進行未預算的資本支出。這些限制可能阻止我們採取對我們業務而言可能有利的行動，並導致我們無法有效應對競爭壓力及產業發展，可能對我們的業務及營運結果造成其他不利影響。

合併的完成受到我們無法控制的條件影響，這些條件可能導致合併無法進行、延遲或以其他方式造成重大不利影響，包括我們股東的批准、適用等待期的到期或終止，以及取得反壟斷及競爭法的相關核准。若合併或類似交易未能完成，我們普通股的股價可能下跌，因為目前市場價格可能基於交易將會完成的假設。此外，根據合併協議所定義的情況，若合併未能完成，我們可能需向波士頓科學公司支付5.25億美元的終止費用。此外，若合併未能完成，可能導致我們在投資界產生負面聲譽。任何因合併公告及待決期間對我們業務造成的幹擾，包括與客戶、供應商、經銷商及業務夥伴關係的任何不利變動，若合併未能完成，這些情況可能持續或加速。我們無法保證若合併未能完成，我們的業務、這些關係或財務狀況不會受到不利影響。
我們因合併而產生了大量法律、顧問及財務服務費用。我們已產生，且預期會持續產生，與滿足合併閉合條件相關的額外費用
